output.summary: KEP-2527 proposed removing or clarifying the "rebuild-from-observation" litmus test for API status fields, acknowledging spec/status as an access-control split, and documenting patterns (such as trusted ACK of spec) for APIs that need controllers to save non-observable state. The KEP is implemented and stable.
output.rationale: The original litmus test ("if I erased the whole status struct, would everything in it be reconstructible from observation?") no longer matches how APIs behave, and it forced reviewers to reject or complicate designs. Spec/status is also used for access control: controllers own status while users own spec, which is why externalIPs was treated as a CVE while LoadBalancer status was trusted. The KEP therefore proposes to drop the test and document an allocation/binding pattern that requires trusted acknowledgement.

alternatives.option: Keep the from-observation rule for status unchanged
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says the ideal 'does not seem to be surviving contact with the real world' and that the rule was a detriment to APIs in review.

alternatives.option: Retroactively apply the new pattern to existing GA APIs
alternatives.why_not: This is an explicit non-goal of the KEP.

alternatives.option: Provide arbitrary storage for controller state
alternatives.why_not: This is an explicit non-goal of the KEP.

alternatives.option: Provide distinct access control for subsets of spec or status
alternatives.why_not: This is an explicit non-goal of the KEP.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes to clarify or remove this guidance, especially as it pertains to state that is not derived from observation.
This KEP further proposes to add guidance for APIs that want to implement an "allocation" or "binding" pattern which requires trusted ACK.
I no longer find this to be useful to our APIs, and in fact I find it to be a detriment.
Unfortunately that ideal does not seem to be surviving contact with the real world.
